questions.prompt: Where should normalisation statistics (mean, std) be fitted?
options: On the test set, so the scaling matches the data seen at deployment
On the full dataset before splitting, so all splits share the same scaling
Separately on each split, so each one is centred and scaled independently
On the training set only, then reused unchanged on validation and test
questions.explanation: Fitting on other splits leaks information; refitting per split changes the transformation between sets.

questions.prompt: What is the correct use of the test set?
options: Early-stop training as soon as the test loss starts to rise
Select the features that look most predictive on the test labels
Tune hyperparameters repeatedly until the test score stops improving
Evaluate the final chosen model once, after all choices are fixed
questions.explanation: Any repeated use for choices turns it into a validation set and biases the final estimate.

questions.prompt: Video frames from the same run end up in both train and test through a random split. What is the consequence?
options: The test score is pessimistic because the model sees fewer frames per run
The test score is optimistic because near-duplicate frames leak run identity
Only the training accuracy changes, since test frames are unaffected
Nothing changes, because consecutive frames of a run are independent samples
questions.explanation: Split by run (group) so the test set contains unseen runs.

questions.prompt: Defects are 1% of parts and missing one is costly. Which report is most informative?
options: Accuracy after adding many more good parts to the test set
Overall accuracy only, since it summarises all parts in one number
Training loss only, since it shows directly how well the model fits
Recall and precision for the defect class, with the confusion matrix
questions.explanation: Accuracy is dominated by the majority class; recall measures missed defects, precision measures false alarms.

questions.prompt: Training targets are 4, 6, 11. What constant minimises squared training error?
A constant prediction of 7 is evaluated on a single test target of 3. What is the squared error?
A test set has 90% negatives. What accuracy (in percent) does always predicting negative obtain?
questions.explanation: It is right on every negative: 90%.

questions.prompt: A detector finds 8 of 10 true defects and raises 4 false alarms. What is its recall?
A model scores accuracy 0.8 on 400 independent test samples. What is the standard error sqrt(p(1−p)/n)?
A model trained on one robot must run on a second robot. Design a split that tests transfer and name two hardware differences that could break it.
rubric: Trains/validates on robot A and tests on unseen robot B (or leave-one-robot-out).
Names differences such as sensor calibration/mounting, actuator dynamics or payload.
Reports performance on the new robot separately, not pooled with the training robot.

questions.prompt: Describe checks you would add to a pipeline to detect leakage: preprocessing order, duplicate samples, group overlap and suspiciously high scores.
rubric: Fit preprocessing inside the training fold only.
Assert group and duplicate disjointness between sets.
Treats a score that is too good as a signal to look for leaks and compares with a baseline.

questions.prompt: A model reports a small test loss. Explain why that is not enough, and what comparison you would add.
rubric: The loss scale has no meaning without a reference.
Adds a trivial baseline (mean/majority) and a simple physical or linear model.
Notes the model must beat the baseline on held-out groups by more than the noise level.
